metadata.script: Perso-Arabic (Dari orthography, ZWNJ U+200C used in prefixes such as می‌)
metadata.verification_summary: All entries are model-generated drafts. NONE has been verified by a native Afghan Dari speaker. Every entry carries verification_status='unverified' until a reviewer confirms it. Do not treat any pronunciation in this file as authoritative before review.
metadata.lookup_key_normalization: Normalize Arabic kaf/yeh (ك ي ى) to Dari (ک ی), apply Unicode NFC, then match with and without ZWNJ and spaces.

pronunciation_guidelines.romanization_system: Afghan Dari pronunciation in Latin characters (AD-Latin v1)
design_principles: Write what a Kabul Dari speaker says, not the letters on the page.
One symbol = one sound everywhere in the file.
Afghan Dari keeps the 'majhul' vowels ē and ō, which Iranian Persian merged into i and u. They must never be written as i or u.
Only lowercase a-z, the macron vowels ā ē ō, apostrophe (glottal stop), hyphen (ezafe/clitic boundary) and space are used.

vowels.note: Final silent-h vowel is 'a' in Afghan Dari, never Iranian 'e' (khāna, not khāne).
Short u-vowel is written o, as in the requested examples raftom, mēkonom.
Distinctive Afghan vowel; Iranian Persian says i.
Distinctive Afghan vowel; Iranian Persian says u.
Iranian 'ow/o' (now, nowruz) is wrong for Afghan Dari.

consonants.note: Afghan Dari uses bilabial/labial-velar w; Iranian v is an error. Some loanwords (vitāmin) vary and are listed as alternatives.
Voiceless uvular stop. Kept distinct from gh. Do NOT merge with غ as Tehrani Persian does.
Word-final h after a vowel is often silent (kolā کلاه, siyā سیاه).
Glottal stop/hiatus in careful speech; usually dropped in colloquial forms (sāat, joma).

consonants.symbol: b p d g k f l m n r
consonants.dari: ب پ د گ ک ف ل م ن ر
consonants.note: As in English; r is a tap/trill.
Used only where the international form is commonly heard; the Afghan w form is listed as an alternative or primary where usual.

rules: R1 Majhul vowels: یای مجهول = ē, واو مجهول = ō (shēr 'lion', rōz, dōst, sēb, mēwa). Never collapse to i/u.
R2 Final silent ه (hā-ye ghayr-malfuz) = a: khāna, hafta, bacha, tāza.
R3 و as a consonant = w (waqt, gāw, keshwar). The connective و between words is -o- (bist-o yak, āb-o hawā).
R4 ق = q and غ = gh are distinct phonemes in Afghan Dari.
R5 خوا is pronounced khā (khāhar, khāndan, khāstan); the و is silent.
R6 Ezafe is written '-e' after consonants and '-ye' after vowels (morgh-e tokhmi, khāna-ye kalān). In fast speech it may weaken; colloquial forms show this.
R7 Present tense prefix می‌ = mē- (stressed). Negative نمی‌ = namē- (stress on na-).
R8 Present endings (standard spoken): -om, -i, -at (3sg, final d devoiced, alt -ad), -ēm, -ēd, -and. Colloquial Kabuli: -om, -i, -a, -ēm, -ēn, -an.
R9 Past endings: -om, -i, ∅, -ēm, -ēd (colloq -ēn), -and (colloq -an). The 1pl/2pl endings use majhul ē (raftēm), not Iranian -im/-id.

R10 Colloquial Kabuli contracts several present stems: رو raw -> r (mērom), گوی gōy -> g (mēgom), شو shaw -> sh (mēshom), آی āy -> y (mēyom), ده deh -> t (mētom), خواه khāh -> khāy (mēkhāyom), آور āwar -> yār (mēyārom), توان tawān -> tān (mētānom), نشین neshin -> shin (mēshinom), فهم fahm -> fām (mēfāmom). These are in colloquial_pronunciation and are high-priority for review.
R11 Copula: است = ast (colloq as / enclitic -a), هستم = hastom (colloq astom), نیست = nēst (colloq nis).
R12 Kabuli words with special pronunciation: شب = shaw, آفتاب = āftāw, خواب = khāw, مهتاب = mahtāw, کبوتر = kawtar.
R13 Stress: nouns and adjectives are generally stressed on the final syllable; verbal prefixes mē-, na-, be-/bo- attract stress; personal endings and the copula are unstressed.
R14 Imperative/subjunctive prefix بـ harmonizes with the stem vowel: bo- before o/u stems (boro, bokon, bokhor), be- elsewhere (begir, bebin), bi- before y (biyā).
R15 Numbers: ده = da, نه = noh, پنجصد = pansad, هفده = hafda, چهار = chār.
R16 Spaces in pronunciation separate words as spoken; hyphens join ezafe and clitics to their host and must not be read as pauses.

pronunciation_fields.pronunciation: Primary standard spoken Afghan Dari form (what an educated Kabul speaker says when reading the written word aloud). Default TTS override.
pronunciation_fields.colloquial_pronunciation: Everyday conversational Kabuli form, if different. Use for conversational/informal TTS style. null when identical.
pronunciation_fields.alternative_pronunciations: Other forms that are genuinely used (formal variants, loanword variants, homograph readings). Not ranked.
pronunciation_fields.regional_variations: List of {variety, pronunciation, verification_status} for Herati, Hazaragi, Panjshiri, Badakhshi, etc.
pronunciation_fields.homograph: true when the same spelling has more than one reading (e.g. شیر shir/shēr, مرد mard/mord). The TTS engine needs context (POS tagger or rules) to choose.
pronunciation_fields.verb_info: For verb forms: infinitive, tense, person, polarity.

tts_integration.overview: Use this file as a word/phrase-level pronunciation override layer in front of the TTS engine's default grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) model.
pipeline: 1. Text normalization: convert digits, dates and abbreviations to Dari words; normalize ك/ي to ک/ی; NFC.
2. Tokenize; attempt longest-match lookup first (multi-word phrase entries such as 'خدا حافظ' or 'تخم مرغ'), then single words. Match keys with ZWNJ/space removed as a fallback.

3. If an entry is found: choose pronunciation by style -> style='standard' uses 'pronunciation'; style='conversational' uses 'colloquial_pronunciation' if not null, else 'pronunciation'. If a reviewed_pronunciation exists in 'review', it takes precedence over both.
4. If 'homograph' is true, choose between 'pronunciation' and 'alternative_pronunciations' using POS/context; fall back to 'pronunciation'.
5. Convert the AD-Latin string to the engine's phoneme set with the mapping table below (longest symbol first: kh, gh, sh, ch, zh, aw, ay before single letters).
6. If no entry is found: run the engine's G2P, but apply the Afghan rules R1-R10 (final ه -> a, و -> w, q≠gh, mē- prefix, majhul vowels where known) instead of Iranian Persian defaults.
7. Optionally filter by verification_status (e.g. only use 'verified' entries in production, use 'unverified' for internal testing).
tts_integration.mapping_note: The IPA column is only an engineering hint for building a phoneme map; it is not a verified phonetic transcription.
tts_integration.example_lookup_code: entry = lexicon.get(key(token)); ph = (entry['review']['reviewed_pronunciation'] or (style=='conversational' and entry['colloquial_pronunciation']) or entry['pronunciation']) if entry else afghan_g2p(token)
limitations: A lexicon fixes word pronunciation only. A natural Afghan Dari voice also needs native Kabul Dari speech recordings and acoustic-model training or adaptation; a voice trained on Iranian Persian audio will keep an Iranian accent even with correct phoneme input.
Prosody, sentence intonation and connected-speech effects across words (ezafe weakening, copula cliticization, vowel elision) are only partly represented.
Generated verb forms follow stem rules; irregular colloquial forms need native review.

review_workflow.goal: Every entry must be checked by at least one native Afghan Dari speaker, preferably a Kabul speaker; poultry/veterinary terms additionally by an Afghan poultry farmer or veterinarian.

verification_status_values.verified: Confirmed by at least one native reviewer (reviewer_id and review_date required).
verification_status_values.verified_multiple: Confirmed by two or more independent native reviewers.
verification_status_values.corrected: Reviewer changed the pronunciation; reviewed_pronunciation holds the correct form.
verification_status_values.rejected: Entry should be removed or rewritten.

review_fields.reviewed_pronunciation: Reviewer's correct primary pronunciation in AD-Latin (null if the draft is correct).
review_fields.reviewer_alternative_pronunciations: Additional genuine pronunciations heard by the reviewer.
review_fields.audio_reference: Path/URL to a recording of the reviewer saying the word (recommended: 16-bit 22.05/44.1 kHz WAV, file name = entry id, e.g. common_0001.wav).

procedure: 1. Sort by review_priority='high' first (contracted verb forms, loanwords, homographs, technical poultry terms).
2. Reviewer listens to/says the word naturally and compares with 'pronunciation' and 'colloquial_pronunciation'.
3. Fill the 'review' object; set verification_status accordingly. Never edit 'pronunciation' directly - keep the draft for audit; the TTS engine prefers reviewed_pronunciation.
4. Record audio and set audio_reference whenever possible.
5. After review, bump metadata.version and recompute metadata counts.
